newsitem.title: GERMANY: German parliament passes sick pay cuts.
newsitem.headline: German parliament passes sick pay cuts.

text.p: The German parliament on Friday approved the government's plans to cut sick pay and reduce workers' protection from firing, a key part of Bonn's austerity drive.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl won an absolute majority for the bill, the second of three keys votes on the austerity package on Friday, overturning objections lodged by the opposition Social Democrat-controlled upper house of parliament on Thursday.

Deputies had already approved Bonn's pension reform bill, which should save around 14 billion marks next year, and were widely expected to pass a health reform bill shortly afterwards that would save around seven billion marks.

While the cuts in sick pay and lowering of worker protection do not save money next year, they form part of the government's drive to reduce firms' costs and deregulate the labour market to encourage new job creation in the longer term.

If the health reforms are also passed, Bonn's austerity package will have taken a major step forward. The bulk of the 70 billion marks of public spending cuts Bonn is seeking for 1997 are now mostly assured.
The government is desperate to get the cuts through to reduce the public deficit sufficiently next year to ensure qualification for the single European currency.
